title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 28 | Week 8 vs. Dallas Cowboys
headline: Michael Wilson's snap share is being managed down with receiver rotation, while Jeremiyah Love is limited but practicing ahead of Dallas.
summary: LaFleur said the team is working to get newly added veteran receiver Zay up to speed quickly, noting that his familiarity with the building and locker room helps. He said Jeremiyah Love will be limited but practicing this week. On the quarterback room, he said rookie Carson is also limited and that the starting job still belongs to Jacoby Brissett, who gives the team its best chance to win. He said the red zone problem needs fixing now, with players told to attack it without freezing up. On Michael Wilson, LaFleur said Detroit's coverage was unusual and that recent defensive adjustments have been mostly scheme-based. He called the drop in Wilson's target share a coincidence, while noting he is a top-eight target leader, and said the team is rotating receivers to keep them fresh over a 17-game season. He credited the rise in deep passes to defenses playing over the top in recent weeks and emphasized explosive plays come from catching and blocking after the catch, not just long throws. He praised Kalen King's toughness and said his arrows are only pointing up. He called Trey McBride's long catch-and-draw play excellent. Looking ahead to Dallas, he said the Cowboys are talented and their defensive line, led by Dan Quinn, is a real strength.

signals.note: Fewer snaps from the early-season every-down role lowers his floor, even with a top-eight target share.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 8 Media Availability | Wednesday, October 28th | Press Conference
headline: Stefanski gave few injury updates for the Week 8 Bucs game, but praised Michael Penix Jr.'s footwork progress and Kyle Pitts' red-zone size and hands.
summary: Stefanski opened by calling Tampa Bay a division opponent and said the injury picture is still in flux. Some players will be limited and evaluated during the week, with a possible return tomorrow, but he gave no specific names or timelines. On offense, he said the Falcons will face heavy boxes and must be able to block them and win with efficiency in the run game, especially against a Todd Bowles defense that also uses heavy boxes and shells. He praised Kyle Pitts' size, elevation and hands, saying vertical separation matters most in the red zone. He called the Buccaneers' defense outstanding and physical, with good scheme and skilled players. On the slow starts, he said the team wants to start fast but the scoreboard matters most. He said Michael Penix Jr. has made progress in footwork, which he tied to completions, and that avoiding sacks and throwing the ball away are positives that don't show up in completion percentage. He also praised Tommy Brick's development as coordinator and described his own role on the headset as supporting one clear voice.

signals.claim: Penix has progressed in footwork, which has contributed to his completions and is being emphasized in coaching
signals.note: Improved footwork and timing could support more efficient passing and completion rates as the starter.
signals.quote: we will always put a huge emphasis on quarterback footwork

signals.claim: Pitts is a strong red-zone target because of his size, elevation and hands
signals.note: Stefanski's praise for Pitts' red-zone profile points to a featured role near the goal line against Tampa Bay.
signals.quote: He's got great size. He can elevate great hands.

topics.detail: Stefanski said the injury situation is fluid. Some players will practice and others will be held out for evaluation, with a possible return tomorrow. He did not name anyone.
Tampa Bay's defense is physical, hard to throw and run against, and has young players and a strong scheme. Stefanski expects heavy boxes and shells from Todd Bowles' unit.

Stefanski acknowledged the Falcons' weak first quarters over the last three games and said the team will keep working on early game plans while stressing that the scoreboard matters more than time of possession.

Stefanski said completion percentage is only one measure and that avoiding sacks and throwing the ball away are important positives. He also said the team prepares for every player on an opponent's roster, including backups.

title: Jesse Minter: Us Against the World Mentality
headline: Lamar Jackson's Sunday status is still unclear, with the Wednesday injury report expected to show how his practice went; right guard is an open competition between Andrew Vorhees and Emery Jones.
summary: Minter called Wednesday's practice good and said the team responded well after its last loss, with a challenge coming Sunday against Buffalo. Asked about Lamar Jackson, he said Jackson got some work in, but he did not give a participation level and pointed to the injury report around 4 p.m. for details. He said that more work and better feel make him more optimistic, but the week will decide. Kyle Hamilton and a few other players sat out practice, which Minter attributed to typical after-game maintenance, and he said he felt good about them. Minter took responsibility for the loss, saying he would have changed play calls and leadership decisions, and said the staff has been working through hard conversations while trying to clear heads. He praised veterans for responding and said the team is emphasizing four-quarter, 'us against the world' play. On the right guard spot, he called the Vorhees-versus-Emery Jones decision open and said the best option will start. He also praised K'Von Wallace and Keondre Jackson for their energy and effort after they got more opportunity, and he welcomed Rayshawn Jenkins for his versatility. Tackling and the run game were key practice focuses ahead of Buffalo's physical, condensed-box running attack and Josh Allen's ability to extend plays.

title: Joe Brady On Improvements After The Bye Week
headline: DJ Moore and Ed Oliver are back at practice this week, with Moore's game status still being evaluated; Keon Coleman is earning more trust and opportunities; Jordan Hancock's IR window is still under review.
summary: Brady said the Bills will use this week's practices to clean up technique and details without losing the things that set the team apart, like effort and running to the football. DJ Moore is back in the mix after sitting out the Monday night game against the Raiders, and Brady hopes to get him on the field today while watching how he progresses. Brady described the bye-week self-scout as a room-by-room tape review on both offense and defense, focused on solutions such as third-down efficiency, scheme and fundamentals. He said the defense shouldn't pin its issues on one position group, and that the safeties, corners and outside linebackers must play within the system and trust each other. Brady praised Keon Coleman's reliability and smarts and said he needs to keep getting opportunities. Ed Oliver is expected to practice today, and Brady said getting him back will help the defense and its identity. Brady also discussed the Ravens, calling Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry a two-dimensional challenge for the defense, and said the team's standings don't matter yet since it is effectively starting over.

title: Zac Taylor: "This Is A Tremendous Opportunity" | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Chase Brown is praised as a key piece of the offense, while Erick All's ACL tear leaves TE and safety depth in question with Russ Yeast and PJ Jules trusted to step up.
summary: Zac Taylor said Erick All tore his ACL and is being supported through rehab, though he described the injury as week to week with a quad issue. He expects other tight ends, including Jack Andrews and a returning Kim Granny, to pick up the slack and said he is not nervous about using Andrews. At safety, Taylor said PJ Jules brings energy and has contributed on special teams, and he feels very confident in Jules and Russ Yeast as depth. On Chase Brown, Taylor praised his approach and said the team will count on him in a big way, crediting him with key plays that keep drives on schedule even without a explosive run yet. He said the team has used two running backs situationally, with the choice depending on the game and down and distance. Red zone success was credited to heavy preparation, with the coaching staff installing concepts early in the week and players adjusting from Friday to Saturday. Taylor said the Browns' Tony Pollard had a big game and that the team is focused on limiting him and other weapons in an offense run by Brian Daboll. He expects Tennessee to be the opponent this week and wants the team to sustain its first-half intensity for four quarters.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference - October 28th, 2026
headline: Deshaun Watson is not practicing Wednesday with knee swelling, but Monken doesn't anticipate him missing Sunday's game against Pittsburgh.
summary: Monken said Deshaun Watson sat out Wednesday's practice because of a little swelling in his knee, and the team wanted to keep him off it. He does not expect the knee to keep Watson out Sunday. On the Steelers game, Monken framed it as a divisional matchup that matters for the standings but said the team's focus is on preparation, not rivalry history or what the win would mean. He said Pittsburgh has evolved since the earlier meeting and that its defense, led by Patrick Graham, mixes interior and edge pressure well. He praised Aaron Rodgers as an elite two-minute quarterback and described the challenge of his high pass volume. Monken credited Watson's belief in himself and the surrounding players for his late-game success, and said he would like the run game to be more efficient so the quarterback isn't carrying the offense. He also said road games are difficult in general and that the offense has been inconsistent, with better moments and parts that still need cleaning up.

title: HC Sean Payton on home-field advantage in Week 8: ‘In a game like this, it’s significant’
headline: Payton says Marvin Mims Jr. has earned more touches, but coverage and personnel groupings limit how often he gets them
summary: Payton previewed the Week 8 matchup with the Chiefs, a divisional opponent the Broncos have ample film on, and noted Kansas City's added commitment to the run game. He praised Alex Singleton, who was Defensive Player of the Week and has been playing with strong instincts. On Marvin Mims Jr., Payton said he has been effective on intermediate routes and as a returner and deserves more touches, but that coverage and finding the right personnel groupings are the barriers. He said Pat Bryant and Jaylen Waddle are the receivers currently banged up, without giving details. Payton said the Broncos need to be sharper in tackling and in the run game than in Week 1, and that Seattle's defense is useful crossover film. He said silent snap counts are harder on the road, that the home crowd has been a significant advantage, and that Bo Nix's 62-yard touchdown run came from reading a defense that was focused on the receivers. He also praised Malcolm Roach's growth as a pass rusher and called him consistent and dependable.

title: Campbell on Vikings defense
headline: Kerby Joseph has started running drills and is progressing toward a return, while Ennis Rakestraw is limited to a walkthrough ahead of the Vikings game.
summary: Campbell said Ennis Rakestraw is doing well but is being held out of practice, with a walkthrough planned before the team moves into a short practice. He said a couple of other unnamed players are also being held back to rest. Kerby Joseph is starting his running progression this week after passing each test on his strength, knee, and quad, and Campbell called it a step in the right direction. Joseph still needs live football work with full-speed reps and contact before a return, which Campbell expects to come late this week or early next week. On the Vikings, Campbell praised their defense as among the best he has seen, citing veteran players, communication, and versatility under Brian Flores, and he said they force offenses into costly mistakes. He also described Kevin O'Connell's offense as playing complementary football, with Murray extending plays with his mobility, and he highlighted a strong special teams unit. Campbell stressed that the Lions need poise, patience, and a defense that continues to step up in this home game, which he called a great test.

title: Shane Steichen: Midweek update, Colts at Jaguars
headline: Colts traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner; Jalen Farmer gets a bigger opportunity at guard, Kenneth Harris earned praise at CB, and Cam Taylor-Britt is out for a while but not season-ending.
summary: Steichen said he has deep respect for Nelson and Buckner, calling them elite competitors and the standard for what a football player should be, and said the locker room was hit hard by their departures. He framed the trades as business decisions the team has to live with and said the message to players was to improve daily and step up. He declined to say whether either player requested a trade and called the team's captain setup unchanged at three for now. He praised Jalen Farmer's work ethic and said he is excited for Farmer's opportunity, noting Nelson had been working with him after practice. On the defense, he was pleased with Kenneth Harris's Week 7 performance, including a pass breakup, and said Harris has been strong in practice. He said Cam Taylor-Britt will be out for some time but is not expected to be season-ending. He moved Wednesday's session to a walkthrough to keep players fresh, noting Jacksonville is coming off a bye, and said the quarterback depth chart has not changed. He said the team has to keep focus through outside noise and that the locker room is ready for a road division game against Jacksonville.

title: Andy Reid: 'Look Forward to the Challenge of Playing the Broncos' | Press Conference 10/28
headline: Cyrus Allen's role is expanding for KC, with more work expected again this week; the full squad practiced ahead of the Broncos game.
summary: Reid opened by saying everyone would practice that day and that KC was looking forward to the challenge of playing Denver, which he described as a strong team under Sean Payton that is playing good football. He addressed the practice-squad signing of a kicker at length but gave vague answers, saying the team did its homework, the player had served his suspension, and the kicker had struggled recently. Reid said the kicker would likely play in the coming game and that he had not seen a scenario where both kickers would be active, and that the veteran kicker was working on technique and consistency. title: Jim Harbaugh on Offensive Adjustments Following the Bye Week
headline: Harbaugh says the bye-week offensive review was about efficiency, keeps OC Mike McDaniel, and calls Joe Alt's possible return a big boost; Derwin James may head to IR.
summary: Harbaugh said the bye week involved a full review of offense, defense, and special teams, with self-scouting aimed at making the offense more efficient across normal downs, third down, red zone, short yardage, goal line, two-minute, and pass and run situations. He described the process as player and staff input through group, position, and unit meetings, and framed the goal as getting a percent better in each situation. He said Mike McDaniel remains the offensive coordinator and expressed strong confidence in him and his system, which he said was familiar to him and something he wanted for the program. Harbaugh did not give specifics on schematic changes. On injuries, he said Brenen Thompson and Deane Leonard would not practice or remained in concussion protocol, Khalil Mack would get a rest day, and Derwin James had a rehab setback that could lead to IR. Ladd McConkey remained in the concussion protocol but was expected to practice. He said Tre Harris was expected to practice, and that Joe Alt's return would be a big boost to the offensive line. Harbaugh also said the team needs to win and focused on winning the day ahead of the Rams game.

He also said the offense needs to balance the run and pass, avoid turnovers, and create explosive plays. He added that the Lions are stronger with Brian Branch back.

He said he saw no effort problem in the Cowboys loss, explaining that every play is graded on assignment and effort in both games and practices, though no team plays a perfect game. On the pass rush, he acknowledged the team could have done more to affect the quarterback, but he avoided scheme specifics and said the defense has to find a balance with its outside playmakers. He credited the offensive line with solid run blocking and protection through three quarters, but said the fourth-quarter deficit forced a faster, no-huddle approach that disrupted the run game. He said the team's best stretches have come when it runs the ball well and wants to build on that. On the backup QB job, he said Joe Milton II earned the No. 2 spot because of his experience and recent practices, while Cole Payton remains a developing rookie the team still values. He said young players like Makai Lemon, Eli Stowers (returning and getting more run), and Keyshawn James-Newby (contributing on special teams and defense) earn playing time through trust built in practice. topics.detail: Saleh called Cincinnati the best team Tennessee will face all season, citing Joe Burrow's play, the run game under the new O-line coach, and the RPO system. He pointed to the Bengals' high-low coverage tendencies.
Saleh called last week's defensive performance the worst tackling day of the season and an outlier, and said he expects a rebound against Cincinnati.

Saleh said the offense has repeatedly produced fourth-quarter drives that tied or took the lead, but said finishing is still a problem, with the team's one-score record reflecting preparation under pressure.
Saleh said trade questions are part of the job and that players should focus on what they control.
The team signed a punter to the practice squad as a precaution, and Saleh said he has worked with Morstead before.
